resource.title: Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets - Instructions for use

text.div:
Synthetic example. Sakura Bloom and Sakuramil are fictitious. This text was written for a FHIR ePI demonstration and must not be used for any clinical purpose.

Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets
Opening the bottle and taking your tablet

For the 30-tablet bottle with a child-resistant cap. Read these steps the first time you open a new bottle.

You will need: the bottle and a glass of water.
Check the expiry date on the label and that the cap has not been opened.
Press the cap down firmly and, while pressing, turn it anticlockwise to open.
The first time only, peel off the foil seal using the tab. Do not use the bottle if the seal is broken.
Tip one tablet into your hand. Check it is pale red, round and marked SB.
Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water, with or without food. Do not crush or chew it.
Turn the cap clockwise until it clicks, so children cannot open it. Keep the bottle out of the sight and reach of children.

text.div: Ask your pharmacist about other ways to open it. Do not move the tablets to another container. For dosing, missed doses and side effects, read the package leaflet.

valueDosage.text: 20 mg once daily; may be increased to 40 mg once daily after at least 4 weeks. Maximum 40 mg a day.

warning.description: Check blood pressure before treatment and at each follow-up visit, particularly in patients with hypertension.
